# Decision history — pixelkit

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## pixelkit.decision.bidi-behind-feature

### Revision 1 — Bidirectional text reordering lives behind an off-by-default `bidi` feature of liminalkit-text

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.bidi-behind-feature/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-text/**"` · topic `text-direction`

liminalkit-text resolves mixed-direction lines with the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm only when its `bidi` feature is on. The feature adds `unicode-bidi` (levels and visual runs) and `unicode-bidi-mirroring` (bracket pairs), which depend on nothing else. `text::shape_face` then shapes each visual level run separately: right-to-left runs are reversed after substitution one base-plus-marks group at a time and positioned in visual order (`Face::shape_run`), with mirrored brackets, and runs are placed in display order. Clusters keep indexing the logical string so `fit`, `wrap` and the cache are unchanged. With the feature off, or for any line with no right-to-left level, the output is byte-for-byte the old left-to-right path. Independently of the feature, the Unicode direction format characters (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069) are never drawn.

**Context.** The outside review asked for bidirectional text. UAX #9 is too large to reimplement in a crate that advertises having no dependencies, and the crate's default build is for appliances that draw Latin and Thai. The feature boundary keeps the dependency-free default honest while letting a desktop application opt in with one line. The direction controls were drawn as .notdef boxes before, which was wrong for every font, so that fix is unconditional.

**Consequences.** Resolution is per shaped line, not per paragraph, because wrapping produces lines before shaping; neutrals at a line edge can resolve differently than a paragraph-level pass would. Controls measure and edit in logical order, so a text field containing right-to-left text draws reordered glyphs but places its caret at the logical prefix's width: fields are correct for left-to-right text only. Complex-script joining (Arabic initial, medial and final forms) is not provided: the layout module applies the lookups the bundled faces use and does not select lookups by script or feature tag, so that remains the external-shaper decision in @pixelkit.work.text-shaping-fallback.

## pixelkit.decision.device-pixel-rects

### Revision 1 — Controls take device-pixel rectangles; Theme sizes are logical and scaled by the control

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.device-pixel-rects/1` · scope `path "README.md"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-shell/src/scale.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/**"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/**"` · topic `units`

Every Rect a Ui control or the Painter takes is in device pixels, the same pixels the buffer holds and the pointer reports. Layout is written in logical pixels and converted once at the call site: Ui::px for a length, Ui::rect for a rectangle, Scale::rect for a whole logical layout (edges rounded independently so neighbours keep touching). Theme's dimensional tokens (padding, row_height, corner_radius, border_width, focus_width) are logical and every control passes them through Ui::px when it uses them. Theme's two font styles are the exception: Ui::new converts its own copy to device pixels so measurement and drawing share one text-cache key, and Ui::text_style converts a custom style.

**Context.** The README said coordinates given to Ui were logical while the examples converted with Scale::px and the painter worked on device pixels. Inside the ui crate the stated contract (theme tokens logical) was applied inconsistently: dropdown and toast scaled row_height and padding, while surface, panel, table, tabs, badge, text_field and the form controls used them raw, so panels and tables shrank at HiDPI scales.

**Consequences.** At scale 1.0 nothing changes. At other scales, panels, table rows, borders and corner radii now follow the scale. A downstream screen that reads ui.theme.row_height still gets a logical value and scales it itself, as the dropdown instructions in the README already assumed. The ui gallery example takes a scale factor so the contract can be eyeballed at 2x.

## pixelkit.decision.facade-crate-and-app-adapter

### Revision 1 — A top-level `liminalkit` crate is the entry point: re-exports, App/Screen adapter, and the cross-crate examples

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.facade-crate-and-app-adapter/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-windowing/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/**"` · topic `entry-point`

crates/liminalkit is the front door. It re-exports the six component crates as liminalkit::{raster, text, shell, ui, windowing} (kms behind a `kms` feature), offers a prelude, and adds liminalkit::app: a Screen trait (one required method, draw(&mut Ui, &mut Context)) and an App<S: Screen> that implements PixelApp, owning the TextCache, RasterKernel, Input, Focus and TouchPointer, forwarding every host event, attaching Tab traversal, and calling Input::end_frame. Context carries the frame's requests back to the host (exit, title, fullscreen, cursor, IME caret, reset_focus). PixelApp stays the low-level interface and App's source is its worked example. Examples that need more than one crate (hello, window, window_lowlevel, panes, multi, touch, touch_tuning) live in crates/liminalkit/examples behind required-features = ["test-fonts"]; the dev-dependency cycle between liminalkit-ui and liminalkit-windowing is gone. Features test-fonts, accessibility and kms forward to the component crates.

**Context.** A first-time user had to assemble a painter, text cache, input, kernel, scale and theme and forward six events before drawing a button. The review asked for an optional high-level adapter that keeps the low-level interfaces intact, and for the cross-crate examples to leave the two crates that dev-depended on each other.

**Consequences.** App does not publish an accessibility tree, arbitrate touch gestures beyond forwarding the first contact as a pointer press, or open further windows; a screen that needs those implements PixelApp. Workspace path dependencies now carry a version requirement and every crate has a description and repository, which costs nothing now and is required later if the crates are ever published; publishing itself is not decided.

## pixelkit.decision.popups-claim-input-first

### Revision 1 — Anything that floats claims its input before the background draws and is drawn last

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.popups-claim-input-first/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/dropdown.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/menu.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/overlay.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/tooltip.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/src/app.rs"` · topic `popups`

Dropdown, Menu and Overlay share one contract. The screen owns the popup's state. At the start of the frame, before the Ui is built and before Focus::handle_tab reads the keys, the popup's handle_input takes the clicks, context clicks, scroll and keys that belong to it or that land outside it (Input::take_keys, restored later with Input::restore_keys, which does not start a new interaction epoch), so background controls never act through a popup. At the end of the frame its draw paints it above everything, hands the retained keys to its own controls, and reports what happened. Under App this split is Screen::before_frame and the tail of Screen::draw. A modal Overlay keeps its own Focus so Tab is trapped inside it; a popover is dismissed by an outside click that is swallowed rather than delivered.

**Context.** Immediate mode has no z-order. The dropdown already drew last and claimed first; adding menus, dialogs and popovers each with their own arrangement would have given screens three rules to remember.

**Consequences.** A popup that is drawn without a prior handle_input still works but is not modal for that frame: draw claims what is left. Overlay content registers its controls with the overlay's Focus explicitly (the _focused control variants); the background Focus may also see them register, harmlessly, because the keys it would act on were taken.

## pixelkit.decision.test-fonts-unpublished-crate

### Revision 1 — The Noto test fonts live in liminalkit-test-fonts, a publish = false crate reached only as a path-only dev-dependency

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.test-fonts-unpublished-crate/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-test-fonts/**"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-text/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/Cargo.toml"` · topic `test-fonts`

Noto Sans Regular 2.004 and Noto Sans Thai Regular 2.000 (unmodified fonts-noto-core builds, SIL OFL 1.1, licence text beside them) are the fixtures of liminalkit-test-fonts, a workspace crate with publish = false that exposes latin(), thai(), LATIN, THAI, set() and style(). Every other crate reaches it only as a dev-dependency declared with a path and no version, which cargo drops when it publishes, so no published crate and no application build carries the 550 KB. The test-fonts feature is gone from liminalkit-text, liminalkit-ui and liminalkit; examples no longer need a feature. liminalkit-text's own unit tests include the same files under cfg(test) by relative path, because they need the faces as that crate's own types rather than a dependency's; a published copy of the text crate therefore builds but its unit tests are run from the repository.

**Context.** The owner asked that the fonts be removed from any crate that might be published so they are not roped in later. Keeping the feature with the files excluded would have shipped a feature that cannot compile; a fixtures crate that is never published is the shape cargo supports directly.

**Consequences.** The README quick start embeds a face explicitly, which is what an application does anyway. Dependent crates cannot be cargo-packaged until liminalkit-raster is on crates.io, so the dev-dependency stripping is cargo's documented behaviour rather than something observed here; the package file list of liminalkit-text was observed to contain no fonts.

## pixelkit.decision.versioning-method

### Revision 1 — Before 1.0 the minor version counts API generations, derived from history; the workspace is at 0.5.0

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.versioning-method/1` · scope `path "CHANGELOG.md"`, `path "CONTRIBUTING.md"`, `path "Cargo.toml"` · topic `versioning`

One version for the whole workspace, with every workspace path dependency pinning it exactly. Before 1.0 the number is 0.MINOR.PATCH. MINOR counts API generations: a generation closes when a change lands after which an application had to edit its own code to keep building or behaving the same (a renamed crate, module or type; a changed signature; a changed meaning of an existing call such as units, frame lifecycle or input ownership; a removed feature). PATCH counts releases within a generation that a dependant absorbs without an edit. A generation counts whether or not it was tagged or published, because applications consumed each one from git. 1.0 when a generation has gone through two application release cycles without a breaking change and the publishing question is resolved. The method and the release steps are in CONTRIBUTING.md under Versioning; CHANGELOG.md lists the generations with the commits that closed them.

**Context.** The owner asked that a first published crate not appear as 0.1.0 but reflect the working state, with a number well under 1.0, and asked for a method rather than a pick. Walking all 29 commits gives five generations: 0.1 extraction from restaurant-pos as pixelkit (d02493c, 2026-08-17); 0.2 the shell rework for LegeOS with text input, IME, presenter injection, clipboard and accessibility (merged 7492c49, 2026-09-24); 0.3 the windowing crate split (593e10d, 2026-09-29); 0.4 the rename to liminalkit with the kms host (cccde64, 2026-10-28); 0.5 the adoptability pass of 2026-11-03 (explicit lifecycle, device-pixel contract, generic Focus, popup input contract, the facade, removal of the test-fonts feature). The owner's guess was 'possibly under .5'; the method lands on exactly 0.5.0 because the rename counted as a generation, every import having changed. Counting only generations under the liminalkit name would give 0.2.0; excluding the rename would give 0.4.0.

**Consequences.** The root Cargo.toml and its workspace dependency requirements say 0.5.0. Cargo treats the 0.x minor as the compatibility boundary, so the method coincides with what keeps cargo update safe for a dependant. Every future breaking change opens a new generation and gets a Breaking line in the changelog saying what a dependant edits. The minor number signals API churn, not maturity: 0.5 does not mean halfway to 1.0.
